subject: Heartland Systems — Post-call technical recap & action items
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@heartland-sys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Heartland Systems — Post-call technical recap & action items

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Below is a concise recap from our call, the technical assumptions we confirmed, and proposed next steps so we can size a pilot (and align procurement). I tried to capture both business goals and the nitty-gritty SLO numbers you called out. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Summary of goals / pain points
- Primary goal: real-time underwriting assistant in checkout with sub-200ms p95 generation latency for single-turn scoring (no heavy context) and overall cost containment.
- Pain: current in-house stack spikes to 800–1,200ms p95 under peak, causing visible UX regressions.
- Data sensitivity: PII in prompts — Heartland requires VPC/private deployment option and audit logs for access.

Confirmed workload profile (you confirmed on call)
- Baseline traffic: ~9k requests/day (stable), expected to double in Q4 if pilot succeeds.
- Peak window: 250 requests/sec sustained for 10–15 minute bursts during business hours; steady-state 100 req/sec.
- Token profile: median request ~120 tokens in, ~60 tokens out; peak requests up to 1,000 tokens due to longer context.
- Query type: mix of deterministic classification + few-shot examples for rare cases; quality sensitivity high for top-1 label.

SLO targets you requested
- Latency: p50 < 60ms, p95 <= 200ms (interactive scoring path), p99 <= 400ms as graceful degradation.
- Availability: 99.9% for production traffic.
- Cost target: keep incremental inference cost below $0.015 per request (target to be validated in follow-up).

Suggested deployment topology (initial pilot)
- Dedicated private pool (VPC) for latency-critical traffic with pinned model versions + autoscaling buffer for peaks.
- Fallback path: hosted Redwood models routing (cheaper) for non-latency-critical workloads and during capacity saturation.
- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix and repeated-prompt caching for common templates; TTL ~2h.
- Model strategy: primary: LLaMA-2-13B quantized to 8-bit for balanced latency/quality. Fallback: LLaMA-2-70B quantized to 4-bit for offline batch scoring / QA comparisons.
- Batching policy: low-latency route uses continuous micro-batching (10ms window) to preserve p95; background batch path allows 50–100ms windows to increase throughput.

Performance expectations (rough, to be validated in perf run)
- 13B int8 on a single M60/A100-class instance (dedicated inference box) with micro-batching: estimated ~120–220 requests/sec for short-context (<=200 tokens) at p95 ~150–220ms depending on sequence length and tokenization overhead.
- With KV cache effectiveness (~40% hit rate on common prompts) we expect effective reduction in token generation and improved tail latency.

Action items / next steps (owners & timelines)
- Rishi: share detailed perf assumptions + test harness and attach initial perf matrix (attached). Due: Tue 2027-06-08.
- Marissa: scope a 30-day pilot commercial proposal with estimated committed capacity & billing terms. Due: Fri 2027-06-11.
- Camila: prepare a one-page security checklist (VPC/KMS/audit logs) and draft an MSA redline we can send to Heartland legal. Due: Wed 2027-06-09.
- Alex / Heartland: share a representative sample of anonymized request traces and a list of top 50 canonical prompts to help build the cache rules. Due: Tue 2027-06-09.

Attachments: heartland-systems-inference-metrics.xlsx (sample perf sheet), redwood-topology-proposal-heatmap.png

If that looks right I’ll queue a perf run with Marissa and schedule a 60–90 minute deep-dive next week with our infra team to go over topology.

Thanks —
Rishi

Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Heartland Systems — Post-call technical recap & action items

Rishi — thanks for the thorough write-up. A few clarifications and questions from our infra/ML lead: 

1) Throughput: the 250 req/sec is accurate for our busiest 15-minute window; sustained baseline is closer to 95–110 req/sec.
2) Token budget: most important scoring uses short prompts (~50–150 tokens), but we have a minority of heavy-context requests (up to ~1k). Can you include tail-case latency expectations for those larger prompts?
3) Quantization: you recommended 8-bit for primary. What kind of top-1 accuracy degradation should we expect if we go to 4-bit for cost reasons? Any A/B guidance?
4) Canary: we’re comfortable with a 5% live-traffic canary but want the ability to automatically roll back on quality regressions. Can your tracing hooks surface per-request model confidence (or at least token-level logits) to our systems for automated guard-rails?

Also: can you provide a ballpark incremental cost per request for the dedicated pool vs hosted (just a 1–2 line estimate so procurement can budget)?

If you can drop the perf matrix and a short architecture diagram, I’ll put this on our infra calendar for the deeper session.

—Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform Engineering | Heartland Systems
alex.morgan@heartland-sys.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@heartland-sys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Heartland Systems — Post-call technical recap & action items

Alex — great questions. Quick answers up front, then I’ve attached the perf matrix and a sketch of the proposed topology (see attached PNG).

Tail latency for heavy contexts
- Short answer: heavy-context requests (>=800 tokens) will increase p95 significantly. With the two-tier approach above, we expect p95 for 1k-token requests to land in the 600–900ms range on the dedicated pool if no cache hits occur; with prefix caching (when applicable) that can drop to 300–450ms depending on hit size. We’ll validate exact numbers in the perf run.

Quantization & quality tradeoffs
- 8-bit (int8) generally preserves near-floating-point quality for many instruction-following tasks on 13B/70B families with minimal top-1 degradation. 4-bit (int4) can introduce measurable quality drift for some prompts — in our internal evals we’ve seen top-1 accuracy drops in the 1–4% range on classification tasks for 13B->4-bit; larger models (70B) tend to be more robust when aggressively quantized, but cost and latency differ. We’ll add a short A/B test plan to benchmark this with your prompts.

Tracing & rollout controls
- Redwood tracing hooks can export per-request metadata, token counts, latencies, and model variant id. We do not export raw logits by default, but can surface model-confidence proxies (e.g. token-entropy, token-prob summary) for guard-rails. Automatic rollback on quality signals is supported via our rollout policies (canary + metric-based rollback).

Ballpark cost estimates (pilot sizing: 2 x dedicated GPU nodes + autoscale buffer)
- Dedicated pool (VPC): estimate $0.009–$0.015 incremental per short request (assuming 13B int8, 40% cache hit); heavy-context requests cost more (proportional to token count).
- Hosted fallback path: $0.006–$0.010 per short request (multi-tenant pricing, lower commitment).

Attachments included: heartland-systems-inference-metrics.xlsx (perf assumptions + matrix), redwood-topology-proposal-heatmap.png (arch sketch). I’ll schedule the infra deep-dive for Thu 2027-06-10 10:00 PT unless you’d prefer otherwise.

Next steps I’ll take immediately: run a short benchmark using your sample traces (if you can share), and surface exact p95 numbers for both 13B-int8 and 70B-4bit for the three canonical prompts you’ll share.

Thanks —
Rishi
